| [AM.MAN.DEX.TACTILE.GEN.1] <a id="am-man-dex-tactile-gen-1"></a> | **DexTouch-WM｜Visual–tactile world model · Action-conditioned data generation · Human-to-robot touch transfer**<br>[DexTouch-WM: Learning Action-Conditioned Tactile World Models from Human Touch for Dexterous Robot Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.20649v2)<br>Yan Qin, Yue Chen, Wenwei Lin, Shujia Liu, Chuqiao Lyu, Kailun Su, Weiyang Jin, Chenze Yu, Ping Luo, Wenbo Ding, Tianxing Chen, Renjing Xu<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `visuo-tactile-world-model` `action-conditioned-world-model` `synthetic-demonstrations` `data-generation` `human-to-robot-transfer` `shared-tactile-layout` `action-retargeting` `mixture-of-transformers` `anatomy-aware-tokenization` `residual-tactile-prediction` `flow-matching` `policy-evaluation` `wuji-hand-2` `real-world` | DexTouch-WM trains a visual–tactile world model on aligned human and robot touch interactions, generates future video and tactile observations conditioned on existing action sequences to form synthetic demonstrations for robot policies, and supports policy evaluation in imagined environments.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Inputs are initial RGB, bilateral touch, an instruction and a given future 67D pose sequence; outputs are future video and touch. Actions condition the model rather than being its control outputs, and there is no action-generating AE. Humans and WujiHand2 share a sensing layout: 360 taxels recorded per hand, 320 retained as five 4×4 fingertip pads and one 15×16 palm pad. Calibration and IK retarget human motion into robot-space bilateral wrists, two 20-DoF hand configurations and camera motion. A Wan2.2-TI2V-5B video expert and lightweight tactile expert interact through MoT joint attention. Fingertips and palms are encoded separately; tactile predictions are residuals anchored to the initial state. AdaLN supplies action conditioning at each modality’s temporal resolution, with conditional flow matching. Scaling holds five hours of robot data from six tasks fixed while adding up to 100 hours across 50 human tasks, testing held-out robot episodes with disjoint human/robot pretraining task sets. Hardware uses a Tianji arm with a 20-DoF Wuji hand. Four additional tasks support adaptation and downstream evaluation, with separate FTP-1, π₀.₅ or X-VLA execution policies. Synthetic demonstrations retain initial observations and recorded actions from real trajectories excluded from world-model training and replace only future RGB/tactile observations. Comparing 200 real demonstrations with 100 real plus 100 synthetic demonstrations does not establish new action planning or reduced need for source action trajectories. Human-mixed adaptation improves average evaluator consistency, but synthetic-policy training utility varies by policy/task, with some real-robot scores declining; equivalence to all-real training is not established. Code, dataset and checkpoint downloads have not been verified. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.20649v2) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
